stories.title: HDFC Bank's new CEO: ₹35.9 crore a year. SBI's chairman: ₹43 lakh.
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: Mon 12 to about Thu 15 Oct while the comparison is circulating; a second peg when Bagchi takes charge on 27 Oct.
happening: Anup Bagchi, now MD & CEO of ICICI Prudential Life, takes over as HDFC Bank's MD & CEO on 27 Oct for three years, succeeding Sashidhar Jagdishan. The bank's postal ballot notice (reported 8–9 Oct) asks shareholders to approve his pay.

The proposed package is ₹35.9 crore a year: ₹8.97 crore fixed (of which ₹3.32 crore is salary; the rest allowances, retirement benefits and perks) plus a target variable pay of ₹26.92 crore for 2026-27, which is 300% of fixed pay. Of the variable part, ₹8.88 crore is cash (₹4.44 crore upfront, the rest over three years) and ₹18.04 crore is in share-linked instruments.
On top: a joining award of about ₹7.35 crore in share-linked instruments over four years, up to two company cars of up to ₹1.4 crore each, and 700 litres of fuel a month.

For comparison (FY26, as reported): outgoing HDFC CEO Jagdishan ₹28.65 crore including stock benefits; Kotak's Ashok Vaswani about ₹17.2 crore; ICICI Bank's Sandeep Bakhshi about ₹10.6 crore; Bagchi himself ₹7.48 crore at ICICI Pru Life.

SBI chairman CS Setty's FY26 remuneration was ₹43.19 lakh (basic ₹27 lakh, DA ₹15.59 lakh, other ₹60,000), the lowest basic pay among the four big state-bank chiefs; PSU bank pay is set by the government.

Desk arithmetic: ₹35.9 crore is about 83 times ₹43.19 lakh, so at the proposed rate the HDFC CEO would pass the SBI chairman's year in about 4.4 days. The comparison is not like for like: one is a forward target that depends on performance and share prices, the other is pay already drawn.
curiosity_gaps: The viral reels call it a '₹36 crore salary'. His salary is ₹3.32 crore. What is the other ₹32 crore, and does he get it?
SBI's chairman runs India's largest bank for ₹43 lakh. Who decides that, and why do the two banks' shareholders pay so differently?
Bagchi earned ₹7.48 crore last year. Moving across the street multiplies it nearly five times. What is HDFC Bank buying?

vidIQ "hdfc bank ceo salary" (India): under 750 searches a month, competition 14 of 100: people share it more than they search it.
YouTube Shorts on the comparison are all tiny (177 to 3,536 views, 4–32 s static cards since 9 Oct), so the format is open on YouTube.

stories.others_takeaway: Every reel so far is the same static card ('₹36 crore salary vs ₹43 lakh') set to music, and the one that broke out did it on the gap alone. Nobody has opened the ₹35.9 crore: ₹3.32 crore is salary, and three quarters is a target bonus, more than half of which is paid in share-linked instruments, which shareholders still have to approve.

facts.text: Bagchi: fixed ₹8.97 crore including ₹3.32 crore salary; target variable ₹26.92 crore (300% of fixed, about 75% of package) for FY2026-27: cash ₹8.88 crore (₹4.44 crore upfront, rest over three years), share-linked ₹18.04 crore; total ₹35.9 crore; joining award about ₹7.35 crore in share-linked instruments over four years, outside the ₹35.9 crore; two cars up to ₹1.4 crore each, 700 litres fuel a month; starts 27 Oct, three-year term; source the postal ballot notice. FY26: Jagdishan ₹28.65 crore incl. stock benefits, Bharucha ₹26.32 crore, Vaswani about ₹17.2 crore, Bakhshi about ₹10.6 crore, Bagchi ₹7.48 crore at ICICI Pru Life excl. options.

SBI chairman CS Setty FY26: basic ₹27 lakh, DA ₹15.59 lakh, other allowances ₹60,000, total ₹43.19 lakh (excludes retirement benefits); lowest basic among SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda, Canara; Bank of Baroda's Debadatta Chand ₹73.16 lakh; PNB's Ashok Chandra about ₹52.6 lakh; from FY26 annual reports. (Context: a separate PLI of about ₹16 lakh is listed outside this total by HelloBanker; not on this page.)
facts.source: Storyboard18, 29 Jun 2026 (context: older than a week, but it is the annual-report figure every reel uses)

facts.text: Business Standard headline, 8 Oct: 'HDFC Bank's Anup Bagchi set to become India's highest-paid bank CEO' (page blocked to our fetcher; the figures above come from FPJ citing the same postal ballot).

watch_out: Call it a proposed package, not a salary and not money earned: three quarters is a target variable pay that depends on performance, and half of it is in share-linked instruments. Shareholders still have to approve it.
Not like for like: a forward target against pay drawn last year. If the reel uses 83× or '4.4 days', say 'proposed' with it.

Real people: no AI face or voice of Bagchi or Setty. A licensed still (check Wikimedia first) or the bank logos; logos are fine because the reel is about the two banks. Humour on the system (who sets PSU pay), never on either man.
No call on HDFC Bank or SBI shares.
Tests it can carry: the number in frame one (B1), 20–30 s (B2), and a send line inside 12 s (B3): the gap is something people forward to the friend in a PSU bank.

stories.title: Musk now promises 'affordable' Starlink in India, days before Jio's $106 billion IPO
stories.label: HOT
stories.window: Mon 12 to Wed 21 Oct: the RHP is expected this week and the issue is reported to open 21 Oct. Each step is a fresh peg.
happening: New since we sent it yesterday: on Saturday Musk wrote on X, "Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable." He also wrote that competition "would greatly benefit the average citizen in India" and "Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business." He gave no Indian price.
The catch Reuters points out: mobile data in India costs about 8 cents a gigabyte, among the cheapest in the world.
The government denies any bias: the three satellite ventures, Starlink's and Jio's included, are all awaiting final security clearance. Reliance has not responded.

Jio Platforms is targeting a valuation of $106 billion in what would be India's largest IPO (Reuters). Terms are still reported, not filed: anchor about 19 Oct, issue 21–23 Oct, listing about 28 Oct; tracking platforms show an indicative band of ₹1,066–1,118 (not final); up to 27 crore fresh shares, no offer for sale, up to ₹27,500 crore to repay Reliance Jio Infocomm's borrowings (DSIJ, 8 Oct).
curiosity_gaps: Indians already pay one of the world's lowest prices for data. How does a satellite service that needs a dish on your roof get 'affordable' against that?
Musk says Ambani's profits will be lower. Ambani is about to ask the public to buy those profits at a $106 billion valuation. Who's right?
Both Starlink and Jio's own satellite arm are stuck at the same security clearance. So who is actually blocking whom?
measured: Trend meter: HOT ("Starlink India price": 16 YouTube videos this week, 5.4M views, best 50,760 an hour). Abhi and Niyu's 18-min explainer: 1.22M views in about a day. The tracker reads the wider Musk–Ambani story HOT; "Jio IPO" FLAT (10% of the week's news today).
Saturday's new turn has barely been made as a Short yet: the top Shorts on it have under 400 views.

stories.others_takeaway: The fight itself is saturated (millions of views on 'real boss of India'). Saturday's price promise is new and unmade: nobody has set 'affordable Starlink' against the 8-cents-a-GB data Indians already get, or against the $106 billion Jio wants for those profits.

facts.text: Musk on X, Saturday: "Obviously, if Starlink is too expensive in India, no one will buy it, so SpaceX will need to make pricing affordable"; competition "would greatly benefit the average citizen in India by giving them more choices"; "Ambani's profits will be lower, but he is not going out of business"; no Indian prices given; India mobile data about 8 cents per GB; Jio Platforms targeting a $106 billion valuation in India's largest-ever IPO; government denies bias, three ventures incl. Starlink and Jio's awaiting final security clearance; Reliance did not respond.

Indicative band ₹1,066–1,118 from IPO tracking platforms, not final; lot 13 shares; anchor 19 Oct, issue 21–23 Oct, listing about 28 Oct (all reported); up to 27 crore fresh shares, face value ₹10, no OFS; up to ₹27,500 crore to repay Reliance Jio Infocomm borrowings; Reuters' reported size of about ₹37,700 crore doesn't match 27 crore shares at ₹1,118 (about ₹30,186 crore).

watch_out: Musk's 'monopoly' and 'Prime Minister Ambani' are his accusations; the government denies bias. Report them as posts, not facts.
No call on the Jio IPO or RIL shares: not 'apply', not 'skip'. Band, size and dates are reported until the RHP is filed, and sources disagree on the size; say 'reported'.
Musk and Ambani: licensed stills or their own real footage only, Musk's posts as screenshots; no AI face or voice, no words beyond what they posted.
No Starlink India price exists yet; don't quote one.

stories.title: Gauahar Khan sold her Versova duplex for almost double. That's about 5.4% a year.
stories.label: COLD
stories.window: Any day this week (evergreen; the sale was reported 9 Oct). Fits the strategist's 'famous Indian's money decision' series.
happening: Actor Gauahar Khan sold her duplex in Versova Shiv Kutir Co-operative Housing Society, Andheri West, Mumbai, for ₹6.01 crore; the sale was registered on 24 Sep 2026 (registration documents accessed by CRE Matrix, reported 9 Oct).
She bought it in November 2014 for ₹3.2 crore. The report puts the gain at about 88% (₹2.81 crore) in nearly 12 years. The buyers paid ₹36.06 lakh stamp duty. The flat is 2,340 sq ft super built-up.

Desk arithmetic: 88% over about 11 years 10 months is roughly 5.4% a year, before her own 2014 stamp duty and costs and before any tax on the gain, which lower it. It also ignores rent saved or earned, which a fair comparison must count.
Context, older than a week: Akshay Kumar sold two Mulund flats for ₹12.38 crore in mid-2026 against about ₹4.49 crore each in 2017, a reported 38% in about nine years (NewsX).
curiosity_gaps: A celebrity 'almost doubles' her money on Mumbai property. Spread over 12 years, it's about 5.4% a year. Did she win?
Headlines report star property deals as profits. What would the same ₹3.2 crore have become elsewhere, and what does the headline leave out (rent, stamp duty, tax)?
measured: Trend meter: COLD ("Gauahar Khan flat": no news this week; 4 YouTube videos, best 261 an hour). Deep lane: momentum isn't expected.
